newsitem.title: TAIWAN: PRESS DIGEST - Taiwan newspapers - December 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Taiwan newspapers - December 26.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Taiwan press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
CHINA TIMES - Opposition New Party will drop out of National Development Conference.
UNITED DAILY NEWS - Taiwan people are not satisfied with their lives, poll says.
International telephone call rates will be adjusted next month (January).
LIBERTY TIMES - Ruling Nationalist Party and opposition Democratic Progressive Party are expected to reach consensus on freezing provincial elections.
Police find two bloodied gloves at home of suspected murderer of Taoyuan county magistrate and seven others.
COMMERCIAL TIMES - Parliament discusses proposal to require employers to give workers six-month grace period in layoffs.
United States agrees in principle to allow Taiwan Vice President Lien Chan to make transit stop during trip to Nicaragua.
ECONOMIC DAILY NEWS - United Nation reports one billion unemployed people in world.
Exchanges between Taiwan and China will not be influenced by tension stemming from World Trade Organisation entry, Taipei says.
